title: Comparing Data Distributions
seo_title: Grade 7 Comparing Data Distributions Worksheets: Mean, MAD, Median and IQR
standard_text: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability. Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 comparing data distributions worksheets: mean and mean absolute deviation, median and IQR, box plots and dot plots, comparing two groups and differences measured in MADs. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Compare the centers, then judge the difference against the spread.
key_sub: Mean with MAD, median with IQR. Means 2 or more MADs apart show a clear difference.
body_html:
Center and spread

To describe data, give a center (a typical value) and a spread (how much the values vary). Use the mean with the MAD for data without outliers. Use the median with the IQR when there are outliers.

CenterHow to find itSpreadMeaning
MeanAdd, then divide by the countMean absolute deviation (MAD)Average distance from the mean
MedianMiddle value in orderInterquartile range (IQR)Q3 − Q1, the middle half
Example

Find the mean and MAD of 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.

Mean = 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

Distances from 8: 4, 2, 0, 2, 4.

MAD = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4.

Answer: mean 8, MAD 2.4

Compare two groups

Compare the centers, then look at the spread. Divide the difference in means by the MAD: if the means are 2 or more MADs apart, the groups are clearly different.

Example

Means 74 and 82, both with MAD 4. How different are the groups?

Difference = 8.

8 ÷ 4 = 2 MADs.

Answer: 2 MADs apart: a clear difference

Common mistakes

  • Finding the median without putting the data in order.
  • Using the range when the question asks for the IQR.
  • Calling a small difference in means important without looking at the spread.

faq.q: What is the mean absolute deviation?
faq.a: The average distance of the values from the mean. For 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 the mean is 8 and the MAD is (4 + 2 + 0 + 2 + 4) ÷ 5 = 2.4.

faq.q: How do you find the interquartile range?
faq.a: Order the data, find Q1 (middle of the lower half) and Q3 (middle of the upper half), then subtract: IQR = Q3 − Q1.

faq.q: When should I use the median instead of the mean?
faq.a: When the data have outliers or are skewed. The median is not pulled by extreme values.

faq.q: How do I compare two data sets?
faq.a: Compare their centers and spreads. Divide the difference in means by the MAD to see how far apart the groups are.

items.e: Distances from the mean: 5, 3, 1, 1, 3, 5. Their mean is 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

items.q: The mean of 5, 5, 7, 9, 9 is 7. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
items.e: Distances from the mean: 2, 2, 0, 2, 2. Their mean is 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6.

items.q: The mean of 20, 24, 26, 30 is 25. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
items.e: Distances from the mean: 5, 1, 1, 5. Their mean is 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

items.q: The mean of 1, 3, 4, 8 is 4. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
items.e: Distances from the mean: 3, 1, 0, 4. Their mean is 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

items.q: The mean of 11, 13, 15, 17, 19 is 15. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
items.e: Distances from the mean: 4, 2, 0, 2, 4. Their mean is 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4.

items.q: The mean of 6, 8, 8, 10, 13 is 9. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
items.e: Distances from the mean: 3, 1, 1, 1, 4. Their mean is 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

items.q: What does the MAD tell you?
c: The largest value minus the smallest
How far the values are from the mean, on average
items.e: The MAD is the average distance from the mean. A bigger MAD means the data are more spread out.

items.q: Data set A has MAD 2. Data set B has MAD 7. Which is true?
items.e: A larger MAD means more variability.

items.q: Find the median of 3, 9, 5, 7, 1.
items.e: Order them: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle value is 5.

items.q: Find the median of 12, 4, 8, 10, 6, 2.
items.e: Order them: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. The middle value is 7.
Order them: 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23. The middle value is 17.

items.q: Find the median of 40, 25, 30, 35, 45, 50.
items.e: Order them: 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. The middle value is 37.5.

items.q: Find the median of 7, 2, 9, 4, 6, 8, 3, 5.
items.e: Order them: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. The middle value is 5.5.
Order them: 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28. The middle value is 22.

items.q: The data in order are 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 4.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 11. IQR = 11 − 4.5 = 6.5. Not 12: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 10, 12, 15, 16, 18, 20, 25. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 12. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 20. IQR = 20 − 12 = 8. Not 15: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 3. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 10. IQR = 10 − 3 = 7. Not 11: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 31, 35, 40, 42. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 23.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 37.5. IQR = 37.5 − 23.5 = 14. Not 22: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 5, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 7. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 14. IQR = 14 − 7 = 7. Not 11: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 30, 32, 35, 36, 40, 44, 45, 50. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 33.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 44.5. IQR = 44.5 − 33.5 = 11. Not 20: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 4, 7, 8, 10, 14, 15, 17, 20. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 7.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 16. IQR = 16 − 7.5 = 8.5. Not 16: that is the range.

items.q: What does the IQR measure?
c: The spread of the middle half of the data
items.e: IQR = Q3 − Q1, the width of the middle 50%.

items.q: Which measure of center is better when there is an outlier?
items.e: The median is not pulled by extreme values.

items.q: Which pair goes together?
items.e: Use median with IQR, and mean with MAD.

items.q: A box plot shows Q1 = 12, median = 15 and Q3 = 20. What is the IQR?
In a box plot, the box shows…
items.e: The box goes from Q1 to Q3.

items.q: A data set is 2, 3, 3, 4, 40. Why is the median a better center than the mean?
c: 40 is an outlier that pulls the mean up
items.e: The mean is 10.4, larger than 4 of the 5 values. The median, 3, fits the data better.

items.q: Adding a very large value to a data set changes which measure more?
items.e: Every value is in the mean, so one large value pulls it a lot. The median moves little.

items.q: Group A: Class A test scores: 70, 75, 80, 85, 90. Group B: Class B test scores: 78, 80, 82, 84, 86. Compare the means.
c: Group A has the greater mean (82 vs 80)
Group B has the greater mean (82 vs 80)
Group A has the greater mean because it has the largest value

items.q: Two groups have means 80 and 85. Both have a MAD of 5. How many MADs apart are the means?

items.q: Two groups have means 90 and 99. Both have a MAD of 6. How many MADs apart are the means?

items.q: The means of two groups are 1 MAD apart. What does this suggest?
c: The groups do not overlap at all
items.e: The more MADs apart the centers are, the less the groups overlap. About 2 or more MADs suggests a real difference.

items.q: The means of two groups are 4 MADs apart. What does this suggest?
c: The groups are almost the same
The groups are very different with little overlap
items.e: The more MADs apart the centers are, the less the groups overlap. About 2 or more MADs suggests a real difference.
